scope: Static actor-spoofing sweep (no POST executed). Modules: organization (teams, person-directory, reporting-lines, org-chart, manager-scope, organization), project-positions, case-management (cases, me-cases), undo. Reference incident F-WP-1: client-supplied actorId persisted to author/audit columns instead of req.principal.
method: Grepped every *.controller.ts in the four modules for actor-ish fields (actorId, performedBy, changedBy, requestedBy, createdBy, resolvedBy, approvedBy, authorPersonId). For each mutating handler, traced the body value into its service/repo and inspected the Prisma create/update to see whether a client-controlled actor field reaches a DB author/audit column without a req.principal override.

spoofable.clientField: TerminatePersonRequestDto.actorId (optional uuid, validated only as uuid shape; NOT cross-checked against the caller)
spoofable.persistedColumn: EmployeeActivityEvent.actorId — written via prisma.employeeActivityEvent.create({ data: { actorId } }) in EmployeeActivityService.record (src/modules/organization/application/employee-activity.service.ts:35). Also flows as actorId into the position RELEASED transitions and into the (in-memory) AuditLogger.
spoofable.rootCause: Controller passes actorId: body.actorId straight into TerminateEmployeeService.execute; the service never overrides it with req.principal.personId. Sibling handler deactivateEmployee (:82) correctly derives actorId from req.principal — terminate is the outlier.
spoofable.impact: Any HR-role caller can attribute a termination's persisted activity-feed author (and downstream position-release audit actor) to an arbitrary personId.

spoofable.persistedColumn: CaseRecord.updatedByPersonId — written via prisma.caseRecord.update({ data: { updatedByPersonId: authorPersonId } }) in PrismaCaseCommentService.addComment (src/modules/case-management/infrastructure/services/prisma-case-comment.service.ts:40). Also stored as the comment author in CaseRecord.payload.comments[].authorPersonId.
spoofable.rootCause: Controller forwards body.authorPersonId (not req.principal) to caseCommentService.addComment, which uses it as both the comment author and the canonical case updatedByPersonId edit-audit column. No principal override.
spoofable.impact: Any HR-role caller can forge both the comment author and the case's last-editor audit column to an arbitrary personId. This is the same class as F-WP-1 (client actor -> updatedByPersonId).

sound.note: Canonical author columns createdByPersonId/updatedByPersonId are set from actorId = req.principal (CreateProjectPositionService :117-118). body.requestedByPersonId at :220 IS persisted but to the distinct business-data column ProjectPosition.requestedByPersonId ('who requested the role'), validated against personExists/personIsActive — it is NOT the create/update audit author. Not an actor-spoof under the F-WP-1 definition.
actorId + actorRoles sourced from request.principal; no actor field read from body.

All derive actorId from httpRequest.principal.personId/userId. createCase spreads {...request, actorId} but CreateCaseRequestDto has no createdBy/actor field, so principal-derived actorId -> createdByPersonId/updatedByPersonId is authoritative (create-case.service.ts:79,82).
actorId taken from req.principal (organization.controller hard-fails 400 if absent). deactivateEmployee (the terminate sibling) is correct — contrast with the spoofable terminate path.

CreateReportingLineRequestDto carries no actor/author field. assign-line-manager.service uses actorId: command.managerId for an event, but managerId is the legitimate business subject (the manager being assigned), not a client-forged performer, and no createdBy audit column is sourced from a body actor.
actorId = req.principal.personId; 400 if absent. Not body-sourced.

sound.handler: org-chart.getOrgChart, manager-scope.getManagerScope, me-cases.listMyCases, all GET list/detail handlers
sound.note: No writes; me-cases is self-scoped on req.principal.personId.

evidence: person-directory.controller.ts:102 passes actorId: body.actorId into TerminateEmployeeService.execute, whose actorId reaches prisma.employeeActivityEvent.create({ data: { actorId } }) (employee-activity.service.ts:35) — a persistent DB audit column — with no principal override; the sibling deactivateEmployee (:82) correctly uses req.principal. cases.controller.ts:407 passes body.authorPersonId into PrismaCaseCommentService.addComment, which writes updatedByPersonId: authorPersonId to CaseRecord (prisma-case-comment.service.ts:40). Both DTOs (TerminatePersonRequestDto, AddCaseNoteRequestDto) validate only the uuid shape, never that the value equals the caller. All other write handlers across the four modules source the actor from req.principal.
